title: Q3 OKR convergence brief and town micro-agenda v0.1
content:
PURPOSE:

This is a working brief to converge company-level OKR recommendations ahead of the Q3 cadence and to provide a compact micro-agenda for the town-style mini all-hands (30–40m) we plan to run the first week of Q3. Goal: reduce back-and-forth between execs and functional leads so we ship an aligned OKR set by the leadership sync on Aug 9.

SUMMARY (TL;DR):
- Target: 3 company priorities + 4 leading indicators. Keep top-level OKRs tight; cascade examples for Eng/Product/Go-to-market in appendix.
- Town format: 25 minute exec update (3 slides, single slide per priority), 10 minute live q&a, 5 minute call-to-action + slack follow-up thread.
- Critical decisions needed by Aug 5: final company-level KRs, safety/compliance threshold for Private offering, Dedicated capacity discount policy.

CONTEXT / CONSTRAINTS:
- Recent customer feedback and pilot metrics show latency regressions at 99th percentile for long-chat workloads (see linked sheet).
- Sales pipeline requires a clear Dedicated SKU commitment to offer 99% tail latency SLAs for enterprise pilots.
- Budget guide: marketing reallocation allowed up to $300k for Q3 experiments; engineering hiring appears flat.

PROPOSED COMPANY-LEVEL OKRs (draft — short list to iterate)
Objective A: Make inference predictable and economical for production teams
  KR A1: Reduce avg cost-per-1k-token served by 20% for hosted API workloads (baseline = May 2024), measured monthly
  KR A2: Cut 99th percentile latency for conversational workloads (<= 2.5s for seq <= 1024) for 3 model families, verified in perf-canal run
  KR A3: Ship model routing fallback policy with automatic degrade path to quantized variants, adopted by 80% of top-10 customers

Objective B: Increase enterprise adoption of Dedicated & Private options
  KR B1: Close 6 Dedicated contracts (>= $50k ARR each) with committed burst capacity in Q3
  KR B2: Complete 2 Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) including compliance docs and KMS integration
  KR B3: Achieve NPS >= 50 in pilot customers after onboarding (surveyed at 30 days)

Objective C: Reduce operational incidents and improve observability
  KR C1: Decrease SEV1 incidents related to serving runtime by 40% quarter-over-quarter
  KR C2: Ship token-level tracing in Console for top 3 customer accounts and instrument three common failure modes
  KR C3: Run two chaos experiments on Dedicated pools and document fallbacks

NOTES ON KRs: keep KRs numeric, timeboxed. Where possible map to dashboard queries (see linked spreadsheets). Open question: how strictly do we define "top-10 customers" for A3? Suggest: revenue-90th percentile or active monthly ops > 10M tokens.

CASCADING EXAMPLES (quick for functional leads)
- Engineering (Serving Runtime): OKR -> reduce tail latency; KRs -> shipping continuous batching improvements, kernel selection heuristics, better KV cache eviction policies
- Product (Hosted API): OKR -> improve predictability; KRs -> routing control plane GA, per-route SLOs in Console
- GTM (Sales + CS): OKR -> enterprise enablement; KRs -> 6 deal closes, create 3 reference case studies

TOWN (MINI ALL-HANDS) MICRO AGENDA (30–40 min)
1) Intro + 60s housekeeping (Asha)
2) Exec updates (25 min total)
   - Priority 1 slide (6 minutes) — context, 2 headline KRs, one ask of org
   - Priority 2 slide (6 minutes)
   - Priority 3 slide (6 minutes)
   - Quick operational pulse (7 minutes) — incidents, hiring, runway notes (one slide)
3) Live Q&A (10 minutes) — pre-seeded questions + 3 live on mic
4) Call to action + follow-up threads (3–5 minutes) — what teams should do in next 2 weeks

Speaker notes guidance for execs:
- Keep each priority slide to one top-level metric and one concrete action for teams to start next week.
- Avoid product roadmap bullets; focus on choices and tradeoffs.

DRY RUN CHECKLIST (between Aug 2–6)
- Slide deck in /company/allhands/Q3-mini-deck (owner: Daniel) — finalize by Aug 4
- Dry run scheduled Aug 6 10:00–10:45 PT (attendees: execs + comms) (owner: Asha)
- Mic check + streaming test with GA phone numbers (owner: Ops — Kai)
- Slack announcement post drafted and scheduled (owner: Priya)
- One-pager for managers with suggested team sync prompts (owner: People Ops — Liam)
- Backstage contingency: if live Q&A overruns, pre-queue 3 pre-approved responses to top 3 expected questions

COMMUNICATIONS & ARTIFACTS
- Pre-read: 2-page summary (use template in Confluence) — send 48h before town
- Manager prompts: 5 suggested discussion points and calibration checklist
- Post-town: structured feedback form (NPS + 3 open fields); consolidate into spreadsheet (owner: Growth)

RISKS & CONTINGENCIES
- If A1 (cost-per-token) targets look unattainable by Aug 9 due to late perf regressions, propose a temporary reframe: shift part of KR to "cost-efficiency experiments launched" instead of full reduction.
- If Dedicated SLAs cannot be met for tail latency, offer documented fallback (reduced promises + premium support) and accelerate Private pilot onboarding.
- If Exec availability is constrained, run two shorter sessions by region (EMEA/US) and record a curated FAQ.

OPEN QUESTIONS (prioritized)
1) Dedicated pricing: what is lowest acceptable discount for committed capacity? (Finance input needed)
2) Compliance gating for Private: do we require ISO attestation before pilot kickoffs? (Security)
3) Customer definition for "top-10" used in KR A3 — revenue vs tokens? (GTM + Data)

DECISION LOG (what we need decided by Aug 5)
- Final company KRs (A,B,C) and definition of metrics (owner: Asha + Daniel)
- Dedicated SKU visibility and pricing bands (owner: Finance)
- Town format approval and comms schedule (owner: Comms — Priya)

NEXT STEPS (owners + deadlines)
- Aug 2: Draft slides complete (Daniel)
- Aug 4: Pre-read published and shared with execs (Asha)
- Aug 6: Dry run complete + feedback incorporated (Asha/Daniel)
- Aug 9: Leadership sync — final signoff on company OKRs (Exec team)
- Aug 12: Town + post-town survey opens (Comms)

APPENDIX (quick refs)
- Baseline metrics mentioned earlier: see linked spreadsheet (latency and cost baselines)
- Playbook link for town run of show: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Town+Playbooks
- Suggested manager prompts (copy-and-paste):
  * Where in your roadmap can you prioritize a 5–10% perf win?
  * Which customers should be targeted for Dedicated pilots?
  * What support do you need from platform to hit the KR by EoQ?

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING ITEMS (raw)
- Need a concise sentence for the town opener about why we pick 3 priorities (keep organizational attention high).
- Confirm with recruiting on realistic hiring for SRE/infra in Q3 (if hires land, can accelerate KR C1).
- Ask product analytics to produce a one-pager on token distribution by customer for prioritization.

End of file.
